doc.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

chapter: Goodman, Hackett and the World's Greatest Jazz Band
title: Bobby Hackett's solo on String of Pearls
summary: Hackett grew tired of playing his classic solo.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Bobby Hackett — didn’t he play that beautiful solo on “String of Pearls” was it?
He played that beautiful solo and he told me he said, “George,” he said, “I got so tired of playing that solo. I’d play it upside down, I’d try to play it sideways, try to play it backwards.”
Isn’t it a great solo? It’s a classic.
It is. It’s like how could you play something better than that?
You can’t improve on it I don’t think.
